question: Mohan can do a piece of work in 9 hours. Pramod can do it in 21 hours. With the assistance of Akshay, they completed the work in 6 hours. In how many hours can Akshay alone do twice the same work
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work (LCM of 9, 21, 6) = 126 units.

Efficiency: Mohan = 14, Pramod = 6, All three (Mohan+Pramod+Akshay) = 21.

Akshay's Efficiency = 21 − (14 + 6) = 1 unit.

Time for Akshay alone to do twice the work = (126 × 2) ÷ 1 = 252 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 252 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Mohan = 9 hours, Pramod = 21 hours, Mohan + Pramod + Akshay = 6 hours.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = Time × Efficiency

**∴ The correct answer is 252 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Individual Efficiency Rule

The efficiency of an individual is found by subtracting the sum of efficiencies of known members from the combined efficiency of the group.

Work and Time Relation

Time is inversely proportional to Efficiency (Time = Work ÷ Efficiency). If work is doubled, time taken at the same efficiency also doubles.</p
